statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 3 and far below the block threshold because CME equity-index futures have been halted since Friday 21:00Z, leaving no Nasdaq-100 price path to score. The last observed path was orderly two-way discovery: Friday's record 31,017.53 intraday high was fully retraced into a 30,807.93 close in the lower quarter of the 30,737.07-31,017.53 session range, with VIX down 6.59% to 15.31. Stress eases to 73, one point below the previous hour, because newly verified weekend evidence partly offsets the unconfirmed Houthi-claimed strike on Aramco's Riyadh refinery: Strait of Hormuz crude flows are reported back near 98% of pre-war levels, the Saudi East-West pipeline and Yanbu loadings have been restored, and the G7 and IEA release of up to 100 million barrels is frontloaded into the next 20 days. Confidence is 85 on verified Friday levels, yields, oil, VIX and a seven-day calendar, with the absence of a live price path as the one explicit completeness gap.
recommendation: Tail stays in the low band for the first eighteen scored hours, so the deterministic mapping remains EA_ON and green through 21:00Z while the weekend halt runs. The three hours from the 22:00Z CME restart carry Tail 21, 22 and 20, which maps to WATCH and yellow: that is the mildest cautionary band and reflects roughly 49 hours of accumulated news repricing into the thinnest books of the week, where a gap can extend without the retracements this framework depends on. Tail returns to the low band at 17 by 01:00Z and eases to 13 by 03:00Z, so the mapping reverts to EA_ON and green for the final three hours. No hour in this window reaches the block threshold, because no persistent one-way Nasdaq-100 structure has been observed and none can be observed while the venue is closed. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unaffected by the mapping.
headline: Weekend CME halt holds Tail at 3 with no Nasdaq-100 price path to score, while verified Hormuz recovery near 98% of pre-war flows and the frontloaded G7 barrel release ease Stress to 73 against an unconfirmed Riyadh refinery strike, keeping the three hours after the 22:00Z restart in the watch band
body:
Friday 2 October remains the last traded session and its levels were independently re-verified for this publication. The Nasdaq-100 closed at a record 30,807.93, up 306.37 points or 1.00% from a 30,501.56 previous close, inside a 30,737.07-31,017.53 session range whose high is also the 52-week high. The detail that matters most for this framework is unchanged: the new intraday record at 31,017.53 was fully retraced and the index finished in the lower quarter of its own daily range. That is orderly two-way price discovery, not the shallow-pullback extension or failed-retracement pattern that defines Tail, so Tail holds at 3. VIX closed at 15.31, down 6.59% from 16.39 inside a 15.30-16.24 range, confirming volatility decay into the halt. Nasdaq-100 futures settled roughly 0.94% higher near 31,049 before CME equity-index trading halted at 21:00Z, and the venue reopens at 22:00Z on Sunday.

The session's driver was the September employment report: nonfarm payrolls rose 29,000 against a consensus near 90,000, the unemployment rate rose to 4.2% from 4.1%, and August was revised down to 133,000. Reporting indicates the probability of an October Fed hike collapsed from 64% to below 21% on that print. The rates reaction was two-way rather than one-way: the 10-year Treasury yield reached 5.34%, its highest since 2002, before retreating to settle near 5.205%, down about 3 basis points on the day. Federal Reserve H.15 data for 1 October shows the 2-year at 4.78%, the 10-year at 5.24% and the 30-year at 5.61%. Yields near two-decade highs alongside a record index level is the central tension holding Stress in the high band at 73.

The weekend's unresolved input is a large fire at Aramco's Riyadh refinery on Saturday 3 October. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree claimed a ballistic-missile and drone strike; neither Saudi authorities nor Aramco have confirmed the cause or any damage, and reporting also describes Saudi strikes on Sanaa. This is the third such episode in 2026 after comparable attacks in August and September, both of which markets absorbed, and the Riyadh site is a domestic refinery rather than a crude export terminal. Set against it is a genuinely verified de-escalation and supply-normalisation thread that this hour's research confirmed: Strait of Hormuz crude flows are reported recovered to roughly 13.2 million barrels per day, about 98% of pre-war levels; Saudi Arabia restarted the East-West pipeline and resumed Yanbu loadings, restoring a Red Sea export route; the G7 and IEA agreed on 2 October to release up to 100 million barrels of crude and diesel over four months with a frontloaded diesel component in the first 20 days and a pledge not to impose energy export restrictions; and weekend remarks attributed to the U.S. president stated that Iran has virtually given up plans for a nuclear weapon and that oil is falling. WTI spot was quoted at $91.11, down 1.90% on 2 October after an intraday one-month low of $88.06, with November WTI futures settling at $93.00 and Brent near $102.25. Oil fell on Friday despite the Gulf headlines, which is itself evidence that the supply-release and normalisation channel is currently dominant.

Two further threads inform Stress rather than Tail. Leadership is narrow: the Nasdaq-100 and the semiconductor complex are firm while the equal-weight S&P, the Dow and small caps are described as still held in bearish intermediate-term downtrends. Under the inherited evidence rules, conflicting breadth reduces directional conviction and raises uncertainty rather than mechanically raising Tail. Separately, a European bond-contagion thread centred on France has the 10-year OAT at 4.924%, its highest since 2002, with the OAT-Bund spread at 1.4 percentage points, the widest since the 2011-2012 crisis. Neither thread establishes a pathological Nasdaq-100 price path.

The shared Finviz context file was read as required and is not usable this hour: its generatedAt is 2026-09-29T23:14:22Z with collectionStatus partial, roughly 4.7 days old and far outside the 90-minute freshness contract. Under the fail-open rule that isolates evidence failure, this publication proceeds on full independent research and the stale context contributed nothing to the scores.

The forward window is shaped by one dated discontinuity. Eighteen of the 24 forecast hours fall inside the halt, where Tail cannot be scored from structure and stays at or just above the floor. The 22:00Z restart repricing roughly 49 hours of accumulated news into the thinnest books of the week is a genuine gap-extension risk, which is why three hours carry watch-band Tail of 21, 22 and 20 and a mixed mode. It is not a block: no persistent one-way structure has been observed, the escalation input is unquantified, the offsetting evidence is verified, and the overlay requires observed mean-reversion failure before Tail crosses 25. The next dated checkpoint after the restart is the ISM Services PMI at 14:00Z on 5 October, with the 10-year auction and September FOMC minutes on 7 October the week's principal rates events.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry published Claude assessments and no slot required an unavailable entry. The window opens at 04:00Z on 3 October with Tail 8 and Stress 65 under a normal mode and decays as the halt takes hold: Tail falls from 8 to 3 by 12:00Z and holds at 3 for the remaining sixteen hours. Stress troughs at 52 around 14:00Z, then climbs steadily to 75 by 02:00Z on 4 October as the energy and Gulf escalation threads reopened and produced the Riyadh refinery fire. Confidence held in a narrow 83 to 88 band throughout, consistent with verified session levels and no live price path. Every slot carried the normal mode and the EA_ON mapping, and no historical opinion was revised with hindsight.
outlookSummary: Eighteen of the 24 forecast hours fall inside the CME equity-index weekend halt, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can form in them. Tail is held at 3 through 15:00Z, then lifts only gradually to 9 by 21:00Z on the restart approach, mapping to EA_ON and green for all eighteen halted hours. The three hours from 22:00Z carry Tail 21, 22 and 20, crossing into the watch band and mapping to WATCH and yellow on a dated discontinuity, the thinnest books of the week and an unresolved Riyadh damage question. Tail then returns to the low band at 17 by 01:00Z and eases to 13 by 03:00Z. Stress runs from 73 down to a 70 trough in the Asian Sunday void, then up to a 78 peak across the restart before easing to 73, remaining in the high band throughout. Confidence decays from 85 to 77 with evidence age through the halt and recovers to 87 once a live price path exists again. The mode is normal through 19:00Z, mixed across the two-sided reopening from 20:00Z to 01:00Z, and normal for the final two hours.
